How does moon simulant and chicken tea affect green bean growth on the moon?
Submitted by: Tyler Cripe, Sean Freund, Brendan Perry, Ezekiel Tabag
We chose to plant green beans in the regolith because after a bit of research of different food
producing plants, green beans were a good plant to use for the experiment since they begin
growing in a short amount of time compared to other plants. We also found out the green beans
can be grown with a variety of other soil besides hardened clay, so we believed it would be able
to grow in the lunar stimulant and the chicken tea. This experiment was valuable because it helps
scientists gather data about plants that could have a chance at growing under the moon's
conditions, which are drastically different compared to Earth.
Our set up was conducted within our science classroom under LED full spectrum lights in room
temperature. Chicken tea is being used as the fertilizer instead of using a chemical fertilizer. We
are using chicken tea rather than a chemical fertilizer because it is a natural fertilizer and it will
limit the amount of variables we have in our experiment. Then we make the chicken tea (take
water and chicken feces, put them in a pillow case, filter the water and throw the pillowcase into
a bucket).
Materials:
●
Full spectrum LED light
●
ISLA’S GARDEN SEED COMPANY (This is where we got the green bean seeds from)
●
Moon soil simulant
●
Burpee: organic coconut coir concentrated seed starting mix
●
Chicken tea (Chicken waste and water and filter it through a pillowcase to make fertilizer)
●
Purified water
Procedure:
1. We took seed starting mix for planting the seed. We took the Regolith (moon soil) and
mixed it 50-50 with our seed starting mix. 100mL of both soils was measured out -
equaling 45 grams of choir and 170g lunar regolith.
2. Make the chicken tea (take water and chicken feces, put them in a pillow case, filter the
water and throw the pillowcase into a bucket).
3. Plant one seed 2 cm under the soil. We planted one seed in each cup (6 seeds). We used
3.5 inch cardboard planting pots.

4. Hang the LED grow light 18 inches above the top of the plant pots
5. Add 40 milliliters of water to the 100 percent water plants (control), 20 milliliters of
water and 20 milliliters of chicken tea to the 50 percent of each (experimental 1-2), and
40 milliliters of chicken tea to the 100 percent chicken tea. (experimental 3-4)
6. Water the plants every week on Tuesday and Thursday. We watered them 40mL of water
for the control. 20mL of water and chicken tea for the 50-50 plants, and 40mL of chicken
tea for the full chicken tea plants.
The reason the experiment was conducted inside in a controlled environment is because it
allowed the plants to be able to be tested with the least amount of outside variables affecting
them throughout the experiment. It was designed this way because it is a lot easier to do the
experiment when you don't have anything affecting them nearly as much. We also used the
coconut choir because it didn’t have additives in it that could help the plant grow. It is just
normal soil with no extra nutrients which helps show how or what the moon soil is doing to the
plant.
Hypothesis: If we add more chicken tea (fertilizer) with the lunar stimulant, then our plants will
be able to grow even under these conditions on the moon. Our team is basically saying that when
more fertilizer is added to the lunar stimulant, then our plants would possibly have a better
chance to grow under the soil and maybe the moon.
Independent Variable: The independent variable within our experiment was the chicken tea,
which is just fertilizer from chicken waste and water that is filtered out and placed in a cup.
Dependent Variable: The height (in centimeters) of the green bean plants was our dependent
variable in the experiment.
Controls: The amount of normal soil and the amount of the lunar soil and the room temperature
was kept the same to isolate the independent variable, which is the chicken tea.
Results: In the end of the experiment, all six of our plants were able to successfully grow with
two of those growing actual beans. Even though some of them were given chicken tea (fertilizer),
it didn’t affect their growth at all by halting it or not having it grow. They were short in the
beginning, but began to grow and were around the same height as the ones without the chicken
tea.

Conclusion:
The results concluded that green beans are able to be grown using moon soil and chicken tea and
without chicken tea as a fertilizer. All the plants with or without the chicken tea all grew
normally and some of them ended up growing beans. What we didn’t expect, however, was that
the leaves began rotting, even when we gave it water and the required chicken tea. Because of
our findings, this tells us that green beans have a possibility of growing on the moon with certain
soil and possibly the fertilizer.
